_licensingNote: Original, not an SCP. This file is an Incident Package manifest — the unit GDD §25.8 states the content-lock gate at — and it binds an anomaly, a map and a premise that are all first-party to this project. licensingRecordId is null because there is no third-party material in the package to record, and this note is what makes that null mean 'checked, and here is why' rather than 'nobody has looked at this one'. §25.7's ShareAlike questions do not engage. The gate status and §25.3's field table are in content/provenance.json.
_note:
THE THIRD FLOOR-SHARE AND THE THIRD PROCEDURE FAMILY AT THE SAME TIME. The cold store now carries three operations: a thing that hunts heat, a thing that stops when you look at it, and a set of objects that does nothing at all. §15.2 wants the building to be the constant and the incident the variable, and by the third one the point is not that the map is reused — it is that a squad walking in already knows where the breakers are, which aisle is the long one, and where the office desk is, and NONE of that knowledge is the answer. Familiarity is the trap.

The stocktake is where they were left, not where they are from. Eleven candidate objects across the floor; five of them are the set. The other six are the same shape, the same weight, and the same colour, because that is the whole incident: a fetch quest is a set where every candidate is real, and this one refuses to be that.

They are placed to make the search gradient do the teaching. Three sit together in the office (aisle-side of the desk, within a metre of each other), so their sinks superpose and the imager reads them from the doorway as one obvious cold patch — that is the squad's first success and it is free. The other two are alone, one at the far north end of the west run and one in aisle C, and a lone object is a two-degree smudge you have to stand over. So the first two minutes are easy and the last ten are work, and nothing decided that except where the objects are.
_spawnNote: The set has no position — presence.field.kind is 'none' and nothing moves. This is required by validateMap and is placed at the head of aisle B where the anomaly object is notionally 'the set', so an operative who somehow reads the debug handle finds it somewhere sensible rather than at the origin.
_variationNote:
GDD §14.4, controlled variation. The bounds are here and the choosing is in code, the same split senses.js makes for triggers: this file says which marks a seed may leave off the floor and where the clerk may be standing; it does not say how one is picked and it cannot introduce an axis.

⚠ NO ORIGIN, NO ROUTES AND NO FAULTS, and all three are refusals rather than omissions.

The origin first. `anomalySpawn` on this incident is a debug handle for a thing with no position, so moving it varies nothing a squad could observe. The axis this incident actually wants is where the eleven objects were left — three in the office, one at the top of the west run, one alone in aisle C, and the search gradient those three placements make — and `instanceSites` is not a variation axis. `chooseVariation` has nothing that touches it, and even if it had, three of the six sources on this floor are the objects' own marks: the frost ring is on the office shelf the three of them sit on, the frost line is beside the one at the north end of the west run, and the aisle C reading is the lone one in aisle C. Moving the set means moving those with it, and the origin and the civilian draws are independent calls to the same generator, so content cannot keep two of them together. That is a change to src/sim/variation.js and it is the single thing that would make this incident vary the way it should.

Then the floor. This level has two doors and two circuits. Three of the five real objects and the stocktake sheet that carries the count are inside the office, and the office has one way in: jam `door-office`, or fault `circuit-office` so the door can never be powered, and the squad is left with a total it cannot reach and two objects it cannot make up the difference with. That is precisely the unwinnable state §14.4 forbids, and it would arrive one night in two with nothing to say it had. Which leaves one safe door and one safe circuit — and `chooseVariation` shuts exactly `routesShutMax` of what it is given, so a one-entry list with a max of one is shut on EVERY seed. That is a permanent change to the floor wearing a variation's clothes. The cold store's stocktake therefore varies in weather, in time, in which mark is missing and in the clerk, and in nothing else.

⚠ `maintenance-log` AND `battery-drain` ARE NOT DROPPABLE. The sheet is the count and there is no second copy of it; a squad that never reads it does not know when it has finished, whatever else the seed leaves lying about. The torches stay off the list for a smaller reason — they are this incident's declared false lead, and `droppable` and `falseLeads` are kept disjoint here as they are in the other four packages, so that a seed never removes the thing it just nominated.

The rest of the list is safe by counting rather than by care. Every rule this floor places now has at least two paths that can be walked to — `first-logged` two, `account-closed` three, `adulterated` two since the stair was put back (see the placement note) — and `dropMax` is one, so no seed can take the second of anything. That is why `stairwell-draught` can be on the list at all: it is the free observation on the way in, and the seed that lifts it makes a squad find `adulterated` the expensive way, in the bay, with two torches out of the same box.

`thermal-void` IS droppable, which is the opposite call from cold-storage-figure. There the instrument-gated sources are the only things the imager has to point at. Here the imager's work is the eleven objects, all night, so a seed that lifts the aisle C reading costs the squad the confirmation and not the object — the fifth one is still standing there, two degrees under the room, waiting to be stood over.

The clerk moves because she is the second count. Where she is standing decides whether the number is the first thing the squad has or the last, and a clerk who is not keen is a longer conversation for the same sentence.

briefing.headline: Stock discrepancy, cold storage level 2
briefing.report: A stocktake on level 2 was run twice by two different clerks and produced the same wrong number both times. The floor was sealed when the second clerk reported a shelf that was 'cold in a way the chiller doesn't do'. Regional wants the discrepancy recovered, counted, and off the site.

known.text: The second clerk is still on site with her sheet. Site will say where she is waiting.
Nothing on this floor has been reported as moving, and nobody has been hurt.
The count is on the sheet. The site does not know it; the sheet does.
A torch left on the shelf overnight was flat in the morning and one carried off the floor was not.

_sitesNote: ⚠ `label` AND `mundaneLabel` ARE THE SAME STRING ON EVERY ROW, on purpose, and that is not an oversight waiting to be filled in. The prompt reads `Take the brass tally` for one nobody has instrumented and `Take the brass tally — reads cold` for one the imager has confirmed, and the ONLY difference between those two sentences is something the squad did. Giving the real ones a different name would put the answer in the interaction prompt and delete the incident. The two fields exist so that a future set CAN differ if a designer wants the confirmed reading to rename the thing.
_placementNote:
⚠ `stairwell-draught` WAS MISSING, AND THAT WAS A DEFECT RATHER THAN A CHOICE. `ninety-one-tally` ships seven evidence rules and this package placed six of them. The seventh reveals `adulterated` — that a real one bleeds a cell flat and that the case counts what answers — and the only other entry that reveals it is `battery-drain`. So on the floor a squad actually stands on, that rule had exactly ONE way to be found. §27.2 asks for two, and one is not a harder rule: it is a rule that a squad who walks past a single pickup can never learn at all, with nothing anywhere to tell them they missed it. AC1c in tools/m0-tests.js counts discovery paths per PACKAGE rather than per anomaly for this reason, and this floor was the last entry on its list.

It is at the head of the stair because that is where a stair draught is, and because the squad walks within a couple of metres of it in the first ten seconds off the steps. That is the shape `adulterated` wants: one path free on the way in, and the other — two torches out of the same box, one left on a shelf overnight and one carried off the floor — twelve metres west into the bay. A seed may lift either, never both.

MEASURED on the shipped geometry, with EVERY door on the floor shut: standable at the 0.34m operative radius; 3.05m to the nearest fixture, which is the extraction point; 4.03m to the nearest other source, `battery-drain`; 4.06m to the nearest place the seed can stand the clerk; 8.80m to the nearest of the eleven objects; and 5.10m to the cargo cache.

IT IS IN THE DOCK RATHER THAN ON THE STAIR ITSELF, and that is forced. The stair head is 3.0m by 3.4m and the extraction point sits in the middle of it: nothing standable inside that room clears 3.0m of it, and a source that close to extraction wins the context verb from the thing a squad is trying to carry a sealed case onto. The east dock is the room the stair head opens into, and it is 3.4m deep — which is why the clerk lost her dock position to this and now waits at the stair head, at the muster board, or down by the office door.
